MINUTES
  REGULAR PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  DECEMBER 18, 2017

A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:15 p.m. in the City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR POPE.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR POPE led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance

3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Chair Pope, Giglia, Persichina, Retz

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Portugal, Romanelli, Wroan

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Heidi Luce, City Clerk

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER GIGLIA

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-D

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAT MINUTES OF OCTOBER 16, 2017

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 8, 2017

C.  JOINT ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL AND PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT
  MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 8, 2017

D.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 20, 2017

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  NONE

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PROPOSED POCKET PARK DESIGN TASKS FOR PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST PARKWAY

  Community Services Director Clark presented the staff report as per the agenda materials noting
  that staff is working with the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy and Harbor Site resident
  John Taber, who offered to make a donation to develop the park, which will be located at Palos
  Verdes Drive East and Harbor Sight Drive. He noted that the proposal from Willdan Engineering
  includes a total of five proposed design tasks for the pocket park; and staff, in consultation with
  the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy, recommends entering into an agreement for the
  first four tasks - eliminating the option of a photographic view simulation for a total amount of
  $13,820.

  In response to COMMISSIONER RETZ regarding the photographic view simulation option, John
  Hildago with Willdan Engineering stated that the photographs of that option that are included in
  the staff report are just an example of what a photographic view simulation consists of.

  In response to COMMISSIONER GIGLIA regarding the cost for the project itself separate from
  the design tasks being contemplated this evening, Community Services Director commented that
  that the project could likely be done at a relatively low cost and those costs would be determined
  once the design is completed.

  1
   In response to COMMISSIONER GIGLIA, Andrea Vona, Palos Verdes Peninsula Land
  Conservancy commented that she has been in recent communication with Mr. Taber regarding
  the donation, and he is still interested in making the donation.

  In response to COMMISSIONER RETZ, Community Services Director Clark commented that staff
  in consultation with the Park and Activities Commission will provide direction to Willdan
  Engineering on the park design specifically taking into account the equestrian trail requirements.
  Mr. Hidalgo further explained Willdan’s involvement in the project. Further discussion ensued
  concerning the timeline for the project.

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA suggested that Mr. Taber be included in the collaborative efforts for
  the design of the park.

  CHAIR POPE expressed sincere appreciation to Mr. Taber for his generous donation in support
  of this project.

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA

  THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION RECOMMEND TO THE CITY
  COUNCIL THAT THE CITY ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH WILLDAN
  ENGINEERING TO COMPLETE THE FOUR PROPOSED DESIGN TASKS TOTALING
  $13,820 AND FURTHER DIRECT STAFF TO CONTACT HARBOR SIGHT HOA
  RESIDENT, JOHN TABER TO REQUEST A DONATION TO THE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION IN THE AMOUNT REQUIRED TO COVER THE
  SELECTED PARK DESIGN TASK COSTS.

  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  AYES:  Giglia, Persichina, Retz and Chair Pope
  NOES: None
  ABSENT:  Portugal, Romanelli and Wroan
  ABSTAIN:  None

B.  HOWLETT PARK BASEBALL LEAGUE REQUEST

  Community Services Director Clark presented the staff report as per the agenda materials stating
  that staff recommends that the Park & Activities Commission approve the Silver Spur Little
  League and Peninsula Junior League’s requests as presented; and approve the conditions of
  sports field use for the new Peninsula Junior League program’s 2018 sports field permit.

  Robert Sinik, addressed the Park & Activities Commission on behalf of the baseball leagues to
  further explain the projects. He also introduce Lucas Hong, Eagle Scout candidate, who will be
  doing some of the project work as part of his Eagle Scout project.

  COMMISSIONERS PERSICHINA and GIGLIA expressed their concern to Mr. Sinik that the
  numbers in the budget he presented for the Peninsula Junior League do not accurately reflect the
  costs associated with George Allen field use, which is considerably lower than reflected in the
  budget according to what they learned in a meeting with officials from the City of Palos Verdes
  Estates. Mr. Sinik explained that he used the numbers that were provided to him and he was
  unaware of the lower numbers.

  Jill Trimmingham addressed the Park & Activities Commission to express concern regarding
  some discrepancies she’s seen in the information provided by the Peninsula Junior League and
  to inquire as to the process for becoming a board member with the organization. In response to
  Ms. Trimmingham, COMMISSIONER GIGLIA explained that the process for electing board
  members for Peninsula Junior League is the same as for Little League.

  CHAIR POPE inquired as to the relevance of the previous discussion and this inquiry in relation
  to the items before the COMMISSION this evening. COMMISSIONER GIGLIA commented that
  his concerns have been sufficiently addressed and he believes the other issues raised will be
  properly addressed by the formation of the new league and are not relevant to the matters before
  the COMMISSION.

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA

  THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION APPROVE THE FOLLOWING ITEMS:
  1) SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE REQUEST TO LENGTHEN THE SNACK SHACK
  STORAGE UNIT’S RAMP BY 36 INCHES AND MAKE IMPROVEMENTS TO THE

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  2
COMMISSION MINUTES
DECEMBER 18, 2017
   SERVICE COUNTER AREA IN ACCORDANCE WITH ADA REQUIREMENT AT THE
  LEAGUES COST; 2) SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE REQUEST TO LENGTHEN THE
  “A” FIELD’S BULLPEN PITCHING WARM UP AREA BY SIX FEET A THE LEAGUE’S
  COST; 3) PENINSULA JUNIOR LEAGUE REQUEST TO INSTALL SUN SCREENS AND
  SHADE TARPS FOR THE DUGOUTS AND BLEACHERS OF THEIR ASSIGNED
  BASEBALL LEAGUE FACILITIES AT THE LEAGUE’S COST; AND 4) APPROVE THE
  CONDITIONS OF SPORTS FIELD USE FOR THE NEW PENINSULA JUNIOR LEAGUE
  PROGRAM’S 2018 SPORTS FIELD PERMIT.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

C.  ROMANIAN FESTIVAL REQUESTS

  Community Services Director Clark presented the staff report as per the agenda materials stating
  that staff recommends that the Park & Activities Commission consider the group’s request to hold
  the 2018 “Romanian for a Day” Festival on Memorial Day weekend and if recommended for
  approval, consider requiring the following conditions: (A) The Festival remain in the same area of
  the park used in 2017; (B) Payment of a $100 per day park use fee, due to exceeding the 100
  maximum attendees for standard Park Permits, for reserving Ernie Howlett Park’s basketball and
  volleyball courts and the picnic area; (C) Payment of any new applicable park fees adopted prior
  to the 2018 Festival; (D) Submittal of a $200 refundable park clean-up deposit; (E) Submittal of a
  Certificate of Insurance to the satisfaction of the California Joint Powers Insurance Authority; (F)
  Obtain a daily State of California Alcohol Beverage Control Permit, with additional insurance
  coverage obtained to the satisfaction of California Joint Powers Insurance Authority; (G) Be in
  compliance with all LA County Health Department Food Service regulations; and (H) Maintain a
  low volume of music, subject to the discretion of park staff.

  Discussion ensued concerning the group’s request to move the event to Memorial Day Weekend
  and to use the sports field area instead of the area used last year. Following discussion the
  COMMISSION concurred that it would best for the event to be held in the same area as last year
  rather than moving to the sports field area as request.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ suggested that the group may wish to use the area where the City
  Celebration is held as an alternative instead of the sports field area.

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ

  THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION RECOMMEND THAT THE CITY
  COUNCIL  APPROVE  THE  ROMANIAN  TRADITIONS IN CALIFORNIA
  ORGANIZATION’S USE OF ERNIE HOWLETT PARK FOR ITS 2018 “BE ROMANIAN
  FOR A DAY” FESTIVAL WITH THE CONDITIONS AS NOTED ABOVE AND THAT THE
  FESTIVAL REMAIN IN THE SAME AREA OF THE PARK USED IN 2017 OR
  ALTERNATIVELY BE HELD IN THE LOCATION WHERE THE CITY CELEBRATION IS
  HELD.
  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

D.  PROPOSED PARK EQUIPMENT RENTAL FEES

  Community Services Director Clark presented the staff report as per the agenda materials stating
  that staff recommends that the Park & Activities Commission adoption of the fees as presented.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ suggested that staff check with the City’s insurance company and City
  Attorney to determine if there are any insurance requirements and to develop a liability waiver.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER GIGLIA

  THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION RECOMMEND THAT THE CITY
  COUNCIL ADOPT THE FOLLOWING PARK EQUIPMENT RENTAL FEES: 1)
  INSTALLATION OF TEMPORARY CHAIN LINK FENCE PANELS - $10/PANEL; 2)
  RENTAL OF 6’ OR 8’ FOLDING TABLES - $10/TABLE; AND 3) RENTAL OF METAL
  FOLDING CHAIRS - $2.50/CHAIR

  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  AYES:  Giglia, Persichina, Retz and Chair Pope
  NOES: None
  ABSENT:  Portugal, Romanelli and Wroan
  ABSTAIN:  None

PARK AND ACTIVITIES  3
COMMISSION MINUTES
DECEMBER 18, 2017
 E.  ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB ESTATES HOA STREET ENTRYWAY PROJECT
  REVISIONS

At the request of the resident proposing the Rolling Hills Country Club Estates HOA street entryway
project revisions, consideration of this item was tabled until the next meeting of the Park & Activities
Commission.

F.  PROPOSED WALL OF RECOGNITION PLAQUES

  Community Services Director Clark presented the staff report as per the agenda materials stating
  that staff recommends that the Park & Activities Commission make a recommendation to the City
  Council to approve the addition of bronze plaques honoring Hope Nolan and Martin Mayer’s
  tenure with the City.

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ

  THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION RECOMMEND THAT THE CITY
  COUNCIL APPROVE THE ADDITION OF BRONZE PLAQUES HONORING HOPE
  NOLAN AND MARTIN MAYER’S TENURES WITH THE CITY.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

G.  NEW RECREATION PROPOSAL

  Community Services Director Clark presented the staff report as per the agenda materials stating
  that staff recommends that the Park and Activities Commission approve the addition of TGA’s
  lacrosse and volleyball camps to the City’s summer recreation program offerings.

  Kiara Williams with TGA addressed the COMMISSION to confirm that their programs are
  designed for children ages 5-12 and they have been getting good participation.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER GIGLIA
  THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION APPROVE THE ADDITION OF TGA
  PREMIER SPORTS LACROSSE AND VOLLEYBALL CAMPS TO THE CITY’S SUMMER
  RECREATION PROGRAM OFFERINGS

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORT – NOVEMBER 20, 2017

B.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORT – DECEMBER 19, 2017

  With no comments or corrections from the Park and Activities Commission, the reports were
  received and filed.

9.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

A.  COMMITTEES, SUBCOMMITTEES AND ADOPT-A-PARK ASSIGNMENTS

  Community Services Director Clark reported that at its January meeting the Park and Activities
  Commission will consider the committee, subcommittee and adopt-a-park assignments for 2018.
  He further suggested formally creating a youth baseball subcommittee and making appointments
  to that subcommittee in January as well.

  COMMISSIONER GIGLIA suggested that rather than limiting the subcommittee to just baseball,
  the subcommittee be a youth sports subcommittee instead. The other members present
  concurred.
